slides.title: Exclusive Ownership with std::unique_ptr
slides.prompt: std::unique_ptr manages heap objects with exclusive ownership semantics. It cannot be copied, only moved, guaranteeing zero-overhead destruction when the owner scope terminates.

slides.title: Creating unique_ptr
slides.prompt: Fill in the recommended C++14 helper function to create a std::unique_ptr safely.

slides.title: Copying std::unique_ptr
slides.prompt: What happens when you attempt to copy pass a std::unique_ptr by value?
options: Compile-time error because copy constructor/assignment are deleted
Runtime crash due to double deletion
Deep copy of the underlying managed object
slides.correctAnswer: Compile-time error because copy constructor/assignment are deleted

slides.title: Transferring Ownership
slides.prompt: Fill in the function used to move ownership from one std::unique_ptr to another.

slides.title: std::unique_ptr Overhead
slides.prompt: What is the memory footprint and runtime cost of a standard std::unique_ptr compared to a raw pointer?
options: Zero overhead: same size as a raw pointer with inline dereferencing
Double size due to internal reference counters
Requires atomic lock operations on access
Allocates hidden tracking headers on the heap
slides.correctAnswer: Zero overhead: same size as a raw pointer with inline dereferencing
